title: TiDB Cloud agent stack: coding-agent platform (Filesystem + TiDB X + Lake)
tagline: Three scripted agent attempts, each with its own copy-on-write workspace and database branch, replayed from a checkpoint and judged in a lake.
pattern: Teams building a coding-agent platform that need an isolated workspace and database per attempt, replayable failures, durable org memory and an analytical store for eval.

nodes.label: Filesystem: base, task layer, attempt layers

metrics.label: Layer Fork Latency
metrics.howMeasured: Wall-clock milliseconds from timed() around one `ti fs fork-layer` CLI call (process start to exit, so it includes the CLI's network round trip). One sample per fork: three attempt forks from the seed checkpoint and one replay fork from a step checkpoint.

metrics.label: Drain plus Checkpoint Latency
metrics.howMeasured: Milliseconds for `ti fs drain-file-system` plus `ti fs create-layer-checkpoint`, each timed with performance.now() inside tiFs.checkpoint and summed. One sample per checkpoint: the seed checkpoint and one per attempt step.

metrics.label: Branch Create to ACTIVE
metrics.howMeasured: Seconds from the runner calling `ticloud serverless branch create` to the first `ticloud serverless branch list -o json` poll that reports that branch ACTIVE. Resolution is the poll interval BRANCH_POLL_MS. One sample per branch: three attempt branches and one replay branch. The vendor documents completion in a few minutes, so expect minutes, not milliseconds.

metrics.label: Hybrid Recall Latency
metrics.howMeasured: timed() around the single reciprocal-rank-fusion query (VEC_EMBED_COSINE_DISTANCE vector list plus fts_match_word list, constant 60, top 3) on the org Starter instance. Sampled once at intake and on every poll of the lesson recall.

metrics.label: Lake Freshness Lag
metrics.howMeasured: Seconds from the runner writing a marker NDJSON object to S3 until a poll (every 3 s) of SELECT COUNT(*) for that marker id in Lake first returns 1. It includes the Lake task schedule (one minute by default), so it is bounded below by the schedule rather than by S3 or the network.

metrics.label: Lake Rows Loaded per Minute
metrics.howMeasured: Live run events visible in Lake (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM run_events WHERE run_id = this run AND source = 'live') divided by the minutes elapsed since the first event object of the run was written to S3. Synthetic history rows are excluded.

metrics.label: Run Events Emitted
metrics.howMeasured: Cumulative count of NDJSON event lines the runner wrote to S3 for this run: one per attempt step, one per attempt finish and one freshness marker.

metrics.label: Run Events Visible in Lake
metrics.howMeasured: Result of SELECT COUNT(*) FROM run_events WHERE run_id = this run AND source = 'live' in Lake, polled every 3 s until it equals events-emitted or LAKE_FRESHNESS_TIMEOUT_MS passes.

metrics.label: Lake Eval Query Latency
metrics.howMeasured: timed() around each of the three eval queries (MATCH on ECONNRESET, merged attempts per dollar by model, COSINE_DISTANCE failure similarity) through the Node driver. Each query opens a new connection, so connection setup is included. Merged per dollar uses synthetic history and fixture model labels, so that result is modeled, not measured.

phases.label: Setup
phases.narration: Three branches of a read-only fixture database start copying now. Branches take minutes, so we ask for them first and overlap everything else.

phases.label: Intake memory recall
phases.narration: Ticket KIT-8812 arrives: fix the double charge on retried payments. Before touching code the agent asks org memory one question that mixes meaning and exact words.

phases.label: Seed checkpoint
phases.narration: The fixture repo lands in a task layer and we checkpoint it as seed. Every attempt starts from exactly this state.

phases.label: Fan out 3 attempts
phases.narration: Three attempts fan out. Each gets a copy-on-write layer forked from seed and its own database branch. Nothing is copied by hand and all three databases start identical.

phases.label: Work loop
phases.narration: Every step is drained, checkpointed, stamped with the branch's own clock and written to the ledger, one second apart so each step lands on a distinct second.

phases.label: Winner PR
phases.narration: The attempt whose tests pass with the smallest change wins and pushes a git branch. Its layer is never committed to the base.

phases.label: Replay the failed step
phases.narration: Attempt 2 failed at step 7. We fork a layer from its step-07 checkpoint, branch its database at that step's timestamp and rerun the step. Same failing tests.

phases.label: Lake eval
phases.narration: Run events and the ledger land in Lake through S3. Now we can search failures, price merged work per model and find failures like this one.

phases.label: Write the lesson
phases.narration: The lesson goes back into org memory. The next ticket that mentions a retry loop recalls it in the first three results.

checks.label: Layer isolation
checks.description: Every file that only one attempt wrote appears in that attempt's layer diff and in no other attempt's layer diff.

checks.label: Fork branches identical
checks.description: The three attempt branches return the same row count and the same row checksum before any step runs.

checks.label: Replay reproduces the failure
checks.description: The replayed step fails the same tests with the same signature, and the replay layer tree and replay branch checksum equal the ledger record of that step.

checks.label: Journal verifies
checks.description: ti fs-journal verify-journal reports the run journal's hash chain intact.

checks.label: Lake count matches emitted events
checks.description: After the load lag, the count of this run's live events in Lake equals the number of event lines the runner wrote to S3.

checks.label: Lesson recalled
checks.description: A hybrid search for a new retry-loop task returns the freshly written lesson in its top three results.

controls.label: Fan out
controls.description: Forks three attempt layers, waits for the attempt branches, runs the work loop and opens the winner's pull request.

controls.label: Inject flaky dependency
controls.description: Before the fan-out: makes attempt 1 hit a gateway connection reset at its first verification so a different attempt wins.

controls.label: Replay failed step
controls.description: Forks a layer from the failed step's checkpoint, branches the database at that step's timestamp and reruns the step.

controls.label: Run eval
controls.description: Exports the ledger, waits for events to appear in Lake and runs the three eval queries.

controls.label: Write lesson
controls.description: Writes the lesson to org memory and checks that hybrid recall returns it.
